newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lacklustre German shares end day lower.
newsitem.headline: Lacklustre German shares end day lower.

text.p: German shares ended a lacklustre day lower, with no clear trend in the market.
Dealers said the market was pausing for breath after surging three percent on Monday, in the absence of new developments to give prices a strong push in either direction.
"There has been no conclusive decision on which direction the market should take next," one trader said.

Dealers said it would be positive for the market if the dollar managed to establish itself above 1.70 marks over the next few days. The market was likely to remain in a holding position in the meantime, traders said.
The immediate direction on prices tomorrow would depend to some extent on whether the 30-share DAX index managed to hold above support at 3,320 points today, traders said.

The index was down 18.54 points at 3,324.23 in post-bourse computer-based trading. It had ended the bourse floor trade session up 16.88 points at 3,329.79, a level which nonetheless was well below the highs seen in late Monday trading.

Features in the market were Commerzbank, which held steady against the slightly bearish tone and BMW, which rose 46.70 marks to 1,346.60. Dealers could give no clear reason for the BMW gains. --Frankfurt Newsroom +49 69 756525
